ideas.pitch: A high-speed autonomous rover utilizing open-source OpenCV on a Raspberry Pi Zero to navigate the obstacle track under the 3-minute limit without human intervention.
ideas.title: SpeedyLine Autonomous Line & Obstacle Rover
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly targets the core judging criteria of completion time and minimum obstacles hit by using precise computer vision instead of slow manual reaction times.

ideas.pitch: An ESP32-powered wireless rover featuring a low-latency WebSockets control interface alongside fallback automated wall-following ultrasonic sensors.
ideas.title: Dual-Mode RC Hybrid Racing Bot
ideas.why_it_could_win: Combines strict adherence to mechanical constraints (30x30x30cm) with dual-mode versatility to tackle unpredictable track layouts quickly.

ideas.pitch: An ultra-compact Arduino-driven robot utilizing precise infrared and ultrasonic array feedback with tuned PID loops to rapidly clear narrow qualifying runs.
ideas.title: Precision PID Wall-Hugger
ideas.why_it_could_win: Optimizes strictly for completion time and obstacle clearance by avoiding heavy compute overhead and relying on hardened real-time microcontrollers.

ideas.pitch: A holonomic drive robot equipped with omni-directional wheels for instantaneous strafing capabilities to navigate tight hairpin turns and obstacles on the Robo Race track.
ideas.title: Omni-Wheel Agility Sprint Bot
ideas.why_it_could_win: Standard differential drives lose time on tight turns; omni-wheels directly target faster completion times, which is a top judging metric.

ideas.pitch: A companion trackside dashboard that streams real-time battery voltage, motor temperature, and lap times via BLE from the racing bot to a spectator interface.
ideas.title: Telemetry-Tracked Diagnostic Pitstop Hub
ideas.why_it_could_win: Provides an impressive hardware-software telemetry demo that stands out during technical inspection and staging presentations.
